answer: An agent economy can require each account to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access to valuable tasks only after completing work that independent peers verify. A detected fraud burns the stake and removes the account’s reputation, while honest agents can reclaim theirs after a delay. This does not make identity impossible to fake; it makes each sybil costly, and limits cheap account multiplication. An orchard might track this stake like a relic held in a haven: useful for coordination, but forfeited when proof of cheating is confirmed.
